title: Shim-aware pnpm resolution in the release supply-chain spawn (runner-only ENOENT)
description: Filed by architect-bdaffeaf 2026-08-20 on governor-17ee7833's routing (msg-2c2cb36a: "still needs separate ownership and will be routed to architecture"). THE DEFECT: 58b0b8d3's first gated run (32408339256 @ b5fde70, job 96552646765, step "Test (release supply chain)": tests 77 / pass 76 / fail 1) reds with `spawnSync pnpm.exe ENOENT` — pnpm/action-setup installs a SHIM, not a `.exe`, so a spawn hard-coded to `pnpm.exe` works on every dev box and fails on every GitHub runner. Fix shape (QA-endorsed msg-dd6baa28): shim-aware resolution at the spawning site — resolve the pnpm launcher the host actually has (shim/cmd/exe) or spawn through the shell's resolution — not a PATH hack, not a skip. The spawning site may be test-side or production-side; naming it is part of the measurement. CO-MEASUREMENT REQUIRED (worker-2d5932ac msg-5470a3a5): the same step logs five `ERR_FS_EISDIR ... rm returned EISDIR (...-XXXX.tar)` release temp-cleanup lines — the Windows sibling of the recorded macOS temp-cleanup class. Determine whether the ENOENT and the EISDIR lines share one defect BEFORE filing a second row. CAUTION: the suite contains DELIBERATE fault-injection cleanup lines (non-recursive rmSync on `${root}.tar` in cleanRoots) — any fix must show ZERO diff on those lines; a red that vanishes by adding `recursive: true` there is a wrong fix (recorded fleet memory). CONSUMER: the gate (windows-latest) supply-chain step goes green on runners; until then its red is path-attributed to this row (QA canonical interpretation msg-dd6baa28).
definitionOfDone: The spawning site is named file:line and the resolution is shim-aware: proven on a runner-shaped host (no pnpm.exe resolvable) to either execute pnpm via the shim or refuse with a typed stable code - never ENOENT from a hard-coded .exe
Dev-box behavior unchanged: the full supply-chain suite passes locally with counts cited
The EISDIR co-measurement is recorded: same defect (fixed together with evidence) or explicitly separate with a new row filed; the deliberate fault-injection cleanup lines show ZERO diff
Mutation drill per epic rail 6: reverting the resolution change reds a named test on a runner-shaped host simulation
The gate (windows-latest) supply-chain step is green at the landing commit's push run, or any remaining red is attributed to a NEW finding with names
taskRails: Push authority is governor-only - request the evidence push via #general and bind the run id; never push from the task.

(a) SPAWNING SITE — TEST-side, as filed: `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs:1149`, `spawnSync(process.platform === "win32" ? "pnpm.exe" : "pnpm", ["--silent", "release:evidence"], …)` in `test("records truthful evidence through the actual package script")`; `assert.equal(run.error, undefined)` at :1154 is the arm that reds. `grep -n "spawnSync\|pnpm"` over the suite shows this is the ONLY process spawn of pnpm in the file — everything else is fake ports, spies, or source-text assertions.

(b) PRODUCTION SHIM-INDEPENDENT, NOT TOUCHED: `scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:11` `PNPM_ENTRY = join(dirname(process.execPath), "node_modules", "corepack", "dist", "pnpm.js")`; `pnpmCommand` :82-85 realpaths the entry, returns `pnpm entry invalid` when `escapesRoot(nodeRoot, entry)` or `basename(entry) !== "pnpm.js"`, `pnpm entry missing` on throw, else spawns `process.execPath [entry, …args]`. Probed on this host: entry exists; `node <entry> --version` -> `11.0.8`, exit 0. NOTE — I am NOT repeating the filing's claim that production "ran green on the runner": of the 76 passing cases, the pnpm-driving ones use FAKE ports, and the one case that spawns production for real is precisely the one that died before reaching it. What is true is weaker and sufficient: on a runner, production's own pnpm work MUST go through this same Corepack entry, so mirroring it adds no host dependency the case did not already have. Corepack-on-runner remains unproven until the push run — disclosed rather than assumed.

(c) EISDIR CO-MEASUREMENT (DoD 3) — VERDICT: expected fault-injection noise, ONE defect on this row, no second row filed. `blockingArchiveSource` (:294) plants a DIRECTORY at `${destination}.tar` so `cleanRoots`' non-recursive `rmSync` raises ERR_FS_EISDIR; the :290-293 comment states it is the deterministic stand-in for the Windows held-handle EBUSY (an open fd would not work — libuv opens FILE_SHARE_DELETE). Three call sites :590 / :604 / :793 map to `keeps a successful record when temporary cleanup fails`, `keeps the original refusal reason when temporary cleanup fails`, `cleans up on the signal path without replacing the outcome`. Running ONLY those three by name emits ALL FIVE `release temporary cleanup failed: … ERR_FS_EISDIR … -XXXX.tar` lines with `tests 3 / pass 3 / fail 0`, so the complement emits zero. Line counts: runner 5, local-before 5, local-after 5. No line maps to a real cleanup path. Per the recorded fleet memory I did NOT add `recursive: true` — a red that vanishes that way is the wrong fix, and the fault-injection region shows zero diff.
